relevance_rank_note: Tests the recycling half of H4 closely (surface LRP1 lost in ApoE4 with normal internalisation, LRP1 stuck in transferrin endosomes, restored by NHE6-driven endosomal alkalinisation) but never measures ApoE-LRP1 binding, so it is B2 by surrogate plus a pH-dissociation perturbation.

description: Raising endosomal pH by expressing NHE6 in ApoE4 astrocytes restored surface LRP1 about 2.5-fold without changing LRP1 transcript or total protein, i.e. relieving endosomal hyperacidification redistributed existing LRP1 back to the surface.
quote: we observed prominent, ∼2.5-fold higher LRP1 staining in ApoE4 cells expressing ectopic NHE6 (Fig. 4F)
system: Immortalised astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic knock-in of human ApoE3 or ApoE4; ApoE4 cells transfected with GFP-tagged NHE6 or empty vector, surface immunofluorescence of non-permeabilised cells, 40 cells per condition. immortalised mouse knock-in astrocyte line, and the comparison is ApoE4+NHE6 vs ApoE4+vector rather than ApoE4 vs ApoE3.
human_check: Class 4: the perturbation acts on endosomal pH (a surrogate for forcing ligand-receptor dissociation), and the readout, surface LRP1, is itself a surrogate for recycling. No ApoE-LRP1 binding is measured anywhere in this paper.

description: Surface biotinylation showed plasma-membrane LRP1 roughly halved in ApoE4 astrocytes relative to ApoE3, with Na/K-ATPase as loading control.
quote: plasma membrane levels of LRP1 are depressed by ∼50% in ApoE4 astrocytes, relative to ApoE3 (**P = 0.0022, Student’s t test; n = 3)
system: Immortalised astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic knock-in of human ApoE3 or ApoE4; cell-surface biotinylation and immunoblot, biological triplicates. immortalised mouse knock-in astrocyte line, not human brain cells.
human_check: Authors print '~50%'; the approximation sign is theirs, recorded as 50%.

description: LRP1 internalisation rate over 10 min at 37 C did not differ between ApoE3 and ApoE4 astrocytes, so the surface loss reflects a return/recycling step rather than faster endocytosis.
quote: No difference in LRP1 internalization was observed between ApoE3 and ApoE4 astrocytes (p=0.2112; n=3; Student's t-test)
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in LRP1 internalisation rate; deficit is at recycling)
system: Immortalised astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic knock-in of human ApoE3 or ApoE4; antibody labelling of an extracellular LRP1 epitope on ice, 10 min at 37 C versus 4 C, flow cytometry, biological triplicates. immortalised mouse knock-in astrocyte line, not human brain cells; panel read from an SI Appendix excerpt transcribed into the local text file.
human_check: Recorded as against because it is a null, though the null is what points the deficit at recycling rather than uptake. The SI legend text in the local file is a transcription of the SI Appendix PDF, not the PMC article body.

description: Endosomal pH in ApoE4 astrocytes was about 0.84 pH units more acidic than in ApoE3, the condition under which ApoE-receptor complexes would be expected to behave differently at the uncoupling step.
quote: Endosomal pH in ApoE4 astrocytes was strongly reduced by ∼0.84 pH unit, relative to ApoE3 (**P = 0.0037, Student’s t test; n = 3)
system: Immortalised astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic knock-in of human ApoE3 or ApoE4; ratiometric pH-sensitive transferrin-FITC with pH-insensitive Alexa Fluor 633-transferrin, biological triplicates. immortalised mouse knock-in astrocyte line, not human brain cells; pH is an upstream condition, not a binding or recycling measurement.
human_check: eff is N/A because a pH-unit difference is not a percent, fold, d or r, and converting it would be a read-off. The 0.84 pH unit shift is stated in the description and quote.

description: Confocal imaging showed LRP1 colocalising prominently with transferrin-labelled recycling endosomes in ApoE4 astrocytes, with loss of LRP1 from processes and perinuclear accumulation.
quote: we find significant colocalization of LRP1 with TFN in ApoE4 astrocytes (Fig. 2G)
system: Immortalised astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic knock-in of human ApoE3 or ApoE4; confocal microscopy of LRP1 and fluorescent transferrin with DAPI, orthogonal slices. immortalised mouse knock-in astrocyte line, not human brain cells; the panel is representative imagery with no quantification of the ApoE3-ApoE4 contrast.
human_check: Fig 2G shows only the ApoE4 condition in the printed panel; no ApoE3 comparison image or quantification is given for this colocalisation, so the contrast is asserted in the text rather than measured. Weak row.
